2. Heard Sri P.Nagendra Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms. K. Priyanka Lakshmi,
learned Assistant Public Prosecutor on behalf of the State.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner is the sole accused.

Earlier,
Crime No.412 of 2020 was registered on the complaint made by Sri V.Ramakrishna Iyer, Vice President, Vasant Chemicals Private Limited on 24.02.2020 in Cyber Crimes Police Station,
Hyderabad.

The Police filed charge sheet, consequently, the Court took cognizance for the offence punishable under Section 66-D of Information Technology Act, 2000 and Section 406 of IPC against the very same accused, who is the petitioner in the present case.
Learned counsel would further submit that the case ended in acquittal, vide Judgment dated 11.09.2024 on the file of XII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Hyderabad.

entities.text: XII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel would further submit that the present case i.e., Crime No. 62 of 2020 is lodged against the Dr.VJPJ, petitioner on the complaint made by Mr. Raghavaiah Gatta, who is the Manager-HR for Vasant Chemicals Private Limited.
The present Crime is registered on 02.03.2020 for the offences punishable under Sections 408, 419, 469 & 471 of IPC and Section 66-C of Information Technology Act, 2000- 2008.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that continuing criminal proceedings against the petitioner amounts to double jeopardy, since the petitioner faced the very same allegations wherein the Court has taken cognizance, conducted Trial and on merits, the case ended in acquittal.
The only difference in the present case is, it was lodged basing on the report of Manager-HR and C.C.No.8790 of 2020 was lodged on the report of Vice President of Vasant Chemicals Private Limited.

4. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor, on verification of the record, fairly conceded that the complaint made against the petitioner in Crime No.412 of 2020 which is numbered as C.C.No.8790 of 2020 which ended in acquittal before the Competent Court is the very same case in the present Crime No. 62 of 2020.
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that Court may pass appropriate orders in this matter.
5. The rule against double jeopardy is solidified by virtue of Section 300 Cr.P.C. and is a manifestation of the auterfois acquit and autrefois convict.
(formally acquitted or formally convicted).
The essence of this doctrine is to see that a person must not be put in peril twice for the same offence.
For the plea of auterfois acquit succeed, it has to be shown that the verdict of acquittal Dr.VJPJ, of the previous charge necessarily involves an acquittal of the latter.

As rightly put by the learned counsel for the petitioner, it was fairly conceded by the prosecution, the petitioner has already faced Trial in C.C.No.8790 of 2020 and was acquitted after full trial vide Judgment dated 11.09.2024 on the file of XII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Hyderabad.
6.

We are also attaching the mail from our customer informing us about the mischievous mail.
Dr.VJPJ, We wish to inform you that all our employees sign a confidentiality agreement and are bound by the confidentiality by terms of our employment.
This mail sent to the customer amounts to Criminal Breach of Trust.
As it is evident from these documents the person has sent this email with an ulterior motive of mischief to damage the business of our company as well as the reputation of our company.

There is an urgency to apprehend such a person as otherwise he will continue to send similar mails to our other customers which will cause irreparable and irreversible damage to our business and reputation.
We request you to kindly treat this as a case of criminal breach of trust and investigate the case and do the needful immediately."

7. The above report was submitted to the Police on 02.03.2020 at 3:00 PM which was registered as Crime No. 62 of 2020 for the offences punishable under Sections 408, 419, 469 & 471 of IPC and Section 66-C of Information Technology Act, 2000-2008.

8. Coming to the case of the prosecution, as can be seen from the copy of the Judgment in C.C.No.8790 of 2020, the following are the allegations made against the petitioner in the charge sheet:

The unknown person has sent this mail with an ulterior motive of mischief to damage the business of the company as well as reputation of the company.

There is a urgency to apprehend such a person, otherwise he will continue to send similar mails to their customers which will cause irreparable and irreversible loss to their business and reputation and requested to take action.
Hence police report."
9. The above crime was registered by Cyber Crimes Police Station, Hyderabad for the offence punishable under Section 66-D of Information Technology Act and 406 of IPC.
The report was submitted to the Police on 24.02.2024 at 11:30 hrs by the Vice President of Vasant Chemicals Private Limited.
As rightly put by the learned counsel for the petitioner, except the name of the complainant in both the crimes, allegations are one and the same.
It is undisputed fact that the petitioner/Accused was acquitted by the Court in C.C.No.8790 of 2020.

Such being the case,
continuing criminal proceedings against the petitioner in the present case is amounting to sheer abuse of process of law.
10. In that view, the petition is allowed.

However, the case against the petitioner in FIR No.62 of 2020 on the file of Rambilli Police Station, Visakhapatnam District registered for the offences punishable under Sections 408, 419, 469, 471 of IPC and Section 66-C of Information Technology Act, 2000-2008 is hereby quashed.
Dr.VJPJ, Consequently, miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
